title: Shetland yoke mittens
subtitle: Full mittens with a two-colour Fair Isle yoke section at the cuff in Shetland tradition.
excerpt: Full mittens with a two-colour Fair Isle yoke at the cuff, worked in DK wool in the round, drawing on the traditional Shetland mitten structure. Plain stocking stitch on the hand and thumb. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Shetland traditional mitten construction with a yoke-style Fair Isle band at the cuff is documented in Michael Pearson's Traditional Knitting (1984) and in Sheila McGregor's Traditional Scandinavian Knitting (1982), both drawing on publicly archived Shetland Museum patterns. The specific motif chart here is adapted from a simple 6-stitch OXF (cross and flower) peerie band which appears in multiple public-domain collections.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stranded colourwork on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A style of stranded colourwork originating in the Shetland island of Fair Isle. Two colours are used per round, with the unused colour carried as a float across the back. Floats should span no more than 5 stitches.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

The cuff has two sections: a 2x2 rib section at the wrist followed by a 10-round Fair Isle peerie band. Above the band, the hand is plain stocking stitch in MC. The construction uses

on a long circular. Budget about 90 g of MC (200 m / 220 yards) and 20 g of CC (44 m / 48 yards), both DK. Swatch in stranded colourwork before casting on: stranded gauge is 1 to 2 stitches tighter per 10 cm than plain knitting.

content.text: Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 42 (48, 48) stitches, a multiple of 6. Join to work in the round. Work 16 (18, 18) rounds of 2x2 rib in MC.
Join CC. Work all 10 rounds of the peerie chart. Drop CC. Work 2 rounds in MC stocking stitch.

Continue in MC stocking stitch for 12 (14, 14) rounds. Place the afterthought thumb: work the first 10 (12, 12) stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and work in MC to end. Continue for 20 (22, 24) more rounds.

Place a marker at the midpoint. Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Remove waste yarn and pick up 10 (12, 12) stitches above and 10 (12, 12) below. Work 16 (18, 18) rounds in MC stocking stitch. Bind off.
Floats too tight across the peerie band: the unused yarn was pulled snug rather than carried loosely. Spread the stitches along the right needle tip before drawing the unused yarn across.
Stitch count is not a multiple of 6: the cast-on was not adjusted before joining. Count carefully before the join; 42 or 48 are the nearest correct multiples for each size.
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Block the peerie section by soaking and pinning flat to dry.
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. Block after washing to keep the Fair Isle section flat.

Full Selbu-style mittens use the same Fair Isle technique across the entire hand and thumb, with a star motif on the back. The Selbu-style mittens pattern is the natural next step from the peerie yoke.
